people.role: Head of Cửu Cao Phái since 1095, crane riders and beast tamers; rider of the crane king Thanh Điền
people.appearance: A wiry, weathered woman with a laugh that carries across the marsh, crane down caught in her braid and a small bronze bell at her belt.
people.backstory: Ung Hạc Minh was born in Hạc Quy Thôn, the village where the cranes come down on the same day every spring, and that year they stayed a month longer (A094). There is no wind in the marsh, and she was born with more Wind than any rider since the founder. Tần Minh Cao (tan_minh_cao) took her up at six and gave her the school when he died in 1095. She has run it the way she runs a flock: loudly, kindly, and from the air. Her riders carry the Pivot's letters to its seven vassals and its envoy to the north, and since Băng Tâm's petition in 1188 her cranes have circled Tinh Tủy Mạch day and night (A096). She flies the night circuit herself once a month with the warden Hình Thủ Tinh (hinh_thu_tinh). In 1197 she tamed the crane king Thanh Điền, which lets no one else on its back and has thrown the Pivot's envoy Vi Thừa Phong (vi_thua_phong) twice (A097). In 1189, to plan the circuit, she opened the school's flight ledger for the years of the vein's first watch.
people.wants: To bring the old cranes home from the vein circuit before it kills them, without failing the Pivot.
people.secret: The founder's flight ledger for 803-806 records Tinh Tủy Mạch flown over every week and found empty: no guard, no fire, no tents. She knows the Pivot's watch was not kept, and she has not told Hình Thủ Tinh, who believes it has never been withdrawn.

people.role: First rider and master of the winter terrace on Thương Ưng Đài, who finds the plateau's Wind children
people.appearance: A silent man in a cloak of crane down who smells of wind and felt, and squints even indoors.
people.backstory: A miner's son from Tập Trận Khoáng, where the wind never stops. Ung Hạc Minh (ung_hac_minh) found him on her first winter on the plateau and he has kept the flock's winter terrace on Thương Ưng Đài ever since. Every winter he walks the hawk-catchers' camps and the mine for Wind-born children. In 1195 he came a week too late for Lộ Khinh Trần (lo_khinh_tran), whom Phất Y's head had already taken. Few of the children he takes come home before the second winter.

ties.note: the skylark girl he found at the hawk camps
the Wind boy he lost to Phất Y; he holds that the boy was promised to the cranes; the boy's letter to Lộ Phi Sương, still on the post road, says the head is teaching him the Step
takes the plateau's Wind children for a sleeve art no one learns

tree.intent: Wind evade and a crane's strike; Earth to stand on the terrace in a gale.
tree.targets_note: Riders' route, then Wind Edge for the crane's strike and the long road to Earthen Gate for footing on the winter terrace.

people.wants: A Wind-born child from the mine this winter, found before Phất Y's head can reach the family.
people.secret: Each winter he tells the families of the children he takes that they will be home by spring, and keeps a tin of the children's toys in his terrace hut, sending one back every year so that it seems true. Mộ Cao Yến (mo_cao_yen) has begun to ask why her mother's toy never came.

people.role: Master of the grooms and the marsh; the strongest cultivator in the school who cannot ride
people.appearance: A slow, broad woman always wet to the knee, with reed cuts on her hands and a crane chick under her arm.
people.backstory: From the carp village of Lý Ngư Thôn, she has bred and fed every crane in the school for eighty years and has never been off the ground, because she has no Wind. She outranks every rider in realm and wears the outer gate's grey. Ung Hạc Minh (ung_hac_minh) calls her the school's mother. She is counting the old cranes the vein circuit has worn out.

ties.note: and friend of eighty years

tree.intent: Wood sustain and binding: the marsh holds the foe while she walks away.
tree.targets_note: Only Beast Den of the riders' route (her root has no Wind), then Reed Shoot, Creeping Vine for the marsh's binding, Willow Dance to walk away.

people.wants: To bring the old cranes home from the circuit to die on the reeds, not the road.
people.secret: She has hidden the three most worn-out cranes in a reed bed no one else knows, so the circuit cannot ask for them again, and Ngụy Hà Lô (nguy_ha_lo), who keeps the second ledger, has written them down as buried.

people.role: The letter rider: flies the Pivot's post to its vassals and the north
people.appearance: A cheerful rider with a satchel of sealed jade tallies across his back and wine on his breath.
people.backstory: A hawk-catcher's son from the windy terrace, he has carried the Pivot's sealed letters since 1170, the same road the riders flew over Phá Quân's fort in 872 (A091). He flies with the Pivot's envoy Vi Thừa Phong (vi_thua_phong) and drinks with him at every vassal's gate. He talks too much and has never once opened a letter.

ties.note: the Pivot's envoy to the vassals; they share a road and a flask

tree.targets_note: Riders' route, then Open Sky Breath and the Riding the Wind idea (Cloud Step, Riding the Wind): speed above all.

people.role: Beast tamer camped below the roc's cliff, who means to ride it
people.backstory: Another child of the windy mine, she has camped under Bằng Sào Nhai for six years feeding the roc goats and waiting for it to let her near; Ung Hạc Minh (ung_hac_minh) thinks it will eat her, and has not forbidden it. She sent her disciple Lộ Phi Sương (lo_phi_suong) into the roc's shadow to feed it first, to see whether it would eat him.

ties.note: rider from Tập Trận Khoáng, Lộ Khinh Trần's cousin, at the roc camp

people.role: Young rider from the hawk-catchers' camps
people.backstory: Cừ Vân Lý (cu_van_ly) found her on the windy terrace catching hawk chicks barehanded; she rode her first crane north to the marsh at twelve and cried the whole way, from joy. She renames her crane every dawn and sulks if the grooms do not use the day's name; Phạm Thanh Lô (pham_thanh_lo) was kept from the dawn feed for saying the old one.

ties.note: rider found on the hawk-catchers' terrace in 1196

people.backstory: Born in Hạc Quy like the head, without her Wind; Mai Lô Tuyết (mai_lo_tuyet) has made him the best groom of his year, and he has stopped asking to ride. He sleeps through the dawn feed three days in seven, and Phạm Thanh Lô (pham_thanh_lo) covers for him and is scolded for the short feed.

ties.note: groom from Ba Quang Thôn, who rows the feed boats

people.appearance: Soft-handed for a groom, and yawning before the sun is fully up.

people.role: Groom from Cự Môn Trấn, of a family that fled Hắc Thạch Trấn in 874
people.backstory: His great-grandmother fled Phá Quân's mining town to Cự Môn when the rebel gate fell (V058) and kept a spearhead and a name she made him promise to hide: Hạ, the Wolf Star's own (ha_lang_tinh). He tells the grooms his family were rope-makers, and when Đậu Quang Lãng (dau_quang_lang) heard the Hạ name from a drunk and asked, he swore the boy had dreamed it.

ties.note: the rebel founder of Phá Quân Môn, by family tale

people.appearance: Never sets his kit-bag down; an old spearhead wrapped in rag lies at the bottom of it.

people.role: Founder of Cửu Cao Phái (700); the first to share breath with a crane of the nine marshes
people.backstory: A Wind-born hawk-catcher of the plateau who followed the cranes north one spring and found where they landed. In 700 he and the first riders shared breath with the cranes of the nine marshes and founded the school (C140, A089). He flew the Pivot's messages over Phá Quân's fort in 872 (A091), kept the school's flight ledger in his own hand for four hundred years, and gave the school to Ung Hạc Minh (ung_hac_minh).

people.cause: brought down by Phá Quân's spears over the rebel fort, carrying the Pivot's message
people.role: Rider who fell over Phá Quân Môn in 872 with the Pivot's letter
people.backstory: One of the riders who carried the Pivot's messages over Phá Quân's fort in the rebellion (A091). On the third crossing the rebels' spears brought her crane down inside the walls. The letter was found sealed on her body when the fort fell in 874 (C163), and Đỗ Tinh Hà (do_tinh_ha) had it delivered unopened. Her crane never took another rider.

ties.note: his spears brought her down

people.appearance: Remembered as a young woman in a slate-grey riding cap, her crane's neck-ring sewn to her cuff.
